name: upper_limb_use
paper_title: A Framework for Sensor-Based Assessment of Upper-Limb Functioning in Hemiparesis
authors: Tanya Subash, Ann David, StephenSukumaran ReetaJanetSurekha, Sankaralingam Gayathri, Selvaraj Samuelkamaleshkumar, Henry Prakash Magimairaj, Nebojsa Malesevic, Christian Antfolk, S. K. M. Varadhan, Alejandro Melendez-Calderon, Sivakumar Balasubramanian
license: Dataset/code: see the source repository. Paper: CC-BY (Frontiers, open access).
notes: 10 unimpaired controls and 5 hemiparetic stroke survivors performed 15 activities of daily living wearing a band on BOTH wrists; therapists annotated upper-limb functional use from video on the FAABOS scale. CODE-VS-DOC: the repository README documents the column layout (time, ax..az, gx..gz, pitch, yaw, mx..mz, subject, old_time, r1, r2, g1, g2, task, use_type, gnd) and 50 Hz; both verified (median clock step 20.000 ms). VERIFIED AT CONVERT TIME: acceleration is in g with gravity present (median |acc| 1.016 g) and angular rate in rad/s (p99.9 6.80). TWO CONVERTER DECISIONS: control and patient cohorts number their subjects from 1 independently, so ids are prefixed c/p to stop them colliding; and the released CSVs do NOT record which side is affected for each patient, so the patient streams are described by impairment (more-/less-affected arm) rather than by anatomical side. Rows with a blank `task` are unlabelled gaps between tasks and are dropped, not relabelled. 682 of 1,042 task runs are shorter than a 6 s window.
